item.title: Color Wheel
item.description:
I apologize for the delay since my last post. Creating a programming language can be a taxing endeavour but it can alo be a lot of fun. I’ve been rewriting LQ in itself (hence the distraction). Along the way I come across some challenges and those challenges lead to some nice solutions.

The Color Wheel

One of the nice things about LQ is the inherent use of iterables. What if you want to create a color wheel. Naturally, you want to iterate through the hues against lightness.

item.title: Control Flow from Closures
item.description:
The previous post ended with a claim: control flow in LQ is just methods that accept closures. No special syntax. No reserved keywords. Conditionals, loops, error handling — all built from the same pieces as any other operation.

This post makes good on that claim. Walking through four fundamental control structures — if, guard, case and try/catch — each one a regular method, each one a small recombination of closures and abutting.
